headline: High: Plandex can write and execute code while ComfyUI is offline-only, creating dangerous shared-workspace and cascading-error risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP bridge, so direct injection is weak. Plandex can read/write a project directory and may ingest ComfyUI outputs if manually bridged through files. The pathway exists mainly via manual copy-paste or shared files, not default automation.
conditions: IF the operator copies ComfyUI-generated text into Plandex prompts or files
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared directory
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs out of Plandex prompt inputs
Use separate directories for images and code
Disable any auto-import of generated text
Review pasted content before sending to Plandex

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory and sends context to a model provider; ComfyUI touches local model assets and can operate offline. If both are placed in the same workspace, source code or generated artifacts can flow into Plandex’s backend. ComfyUI is not the leak source, but the pair creates a default workspace-sharing exposure.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are stored inside Plandex's project directory
IF Plandex is connected to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Store ComfyUI assets outside the Plandex project tree
Use a local-only model provider for Plandex
Restrict Plandex to non-sensitive repositories
Rotate any secrets that were present in shared folders

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI is read-only with respect to filesystem, but Plandex can execute shell, write files, and modify git state. In a shared repo or workspace, Plandex’s writes can collide with ComfyUI-managed assets or user edits, and Plandex supports multiple instances via shared backend state. The overlap is operationally dangerous by default in shared directories.
conditions: IF Plandex and ComfyUI target the same directory
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while another instance is active
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Turn off auto-apply in Plandex
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches for Plandex changes
requires-engineering: add filesystem locking around shared paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a coding agent that can act on generated context, while ComfyUI produces workflows and assets that Plandex could treat as authoritative if manually fed in. Because Plandex can execute shell and modify git state, a mistaken interpretation of ComfyUI output can cascade into destructive code or repo changes. No verification link is documented between them.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are pasted into Plandex as instructions or facts
IF Plandex auto-applies changes derived from those outputs
mitigations: Require human review before Plandex apply
Keep ComfyUI outputs out of code-generation prompts
Use a checklist to verify generated facts
Limit Plandex to staging-only mode

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile shows regulated data handling like PHI or EU-only residency. ComfyUI touches media/model assets; Plandex touches source code and model-provider keys, but no explicit residency or retention mismatch is documented. The other agent is not cited because no compliance conflict is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace
IF a deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees not shown here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workspaces
Document retention settings for Plandex
Store secrets outside project folders
Review vendor data-processing terms
